inspiration: Modular wall kit: a whole dungeon or town is assembled from a small set of flat pieces (wall, raised, edge, ceiling, diagonal, transparent wall). Each piece is a single quad or a couple of quads, and a material name per piece decides the texture. Recreate: 12-15 flat pieces with rotation variants give a lot of variety cheaply.

Palette-index shading: textures are stored as palette indices, index 0 is discarded as transparent, and a light-level lookup table turns the index into a shaded colour. Result: a coherent dim-to-bright look with no per-pixel colour art. Recreate with our own 8-bit palette and our own shade ramp.

Scheduled world clock: one clock file sets lamppost on and off times, ambient brightening and dimming windows, music switching times and a thunderstorm window that spans the night (Clocks.txt lines 18-24). The windows overlap on purpose so dusk feels gradual. Recreate: a day clock driving lights, music and weather together.

Data-declared screens: each UI screen is a text file listing widgets with type, position, pivot, draw order, font and text colour (ui/Automap.txt). New screens need no code change. Recreate with our own schema tuned for phone width and touch anchors.

Light binning on the GPU: a compute shader sorts lights into frustum-shaped bins so each surface only checks nearby lights (LightBinning.comp). Recreate with screen-tile binning instead of frustum planes if we need many torches.

Animated surfaces through a single percent uniform in a screen-space animation pass (OpaqueScreenSpaceAnimation.frag, line 12). Recreate as one time value per frame driving water or lava, with no extra art.

briefs.label: Modular dungeon wall kit
briefs.why: A few flat pieces with per-piece material names make many distinct rooms, so the set reads as a built world rather than a single backdrop.
change: bevelled block proportions instead of flat quads
a corner and diagonal scheme of our own
a different material set, e.g. weathered stone and metal

briefs.label: Palette-indexed torchlit wall
briefs.why: Index-to-shade lookup gives coherent light falloff across all surfaces with one palette and one lookup table.
keep: shade table lookup per light level
change: a cool blue-grey palette family instead of warm earth tones
a different shade count and ramp curve
emissive torch indices kept outside the shade table

briefs.label: Day-to-night clock with lamp and storm windows
briefs.why: Overlapping scheduled windows (lamps, ambient, music, storm) make a town feel alive across a day without a single timeline.
keep: music changes on its own schedule
change: weather as a front that moves, not fixed clock times
lamp timing tied to district, not one global time
music crossfade rather than a hard switch

briefs.label: Declarative HUD screens
briefs.why: Screens are data, so a designer can re-lay a screen without touching code.
keep: widget list with position, pivot and draw order
change: JSON with responsive anchors for phone width
touch-sized hit areas declared in the same file

briefs.label: Light binning for many torches
briefs.why: Culling lights per surface keeps a torch-lit town cheap.
keep: bins built each frame from the camera
change: screen-tile bins instead of frustum planes
fewer, larger bins for low-end phones
